summary: Karpathy coined 'agentic engineering' in Feb 2026 and published AutoResearch, a 630-line ML automation harness where an agent edits training code, runs 5-min experiments, and keeps changes only if validation improves. Also describes a 'programmable layer of abstraction' covering agents, prompts, memory, permissions, tools, plugins, skills, hooks, MCP.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the layered abstraction framing maps to AgentForge's existing architecture; AutoResearch's train-test loop is domain-specific (ML training) not orchestration. AgentForge already ships agent dispatch, skill distillation, and SSE streaming.

summary: Microsoft's open-source successor to AutoGen, supporting MCP and A2A protocols. Offers sequential, concurrent, group-chat, handoff, and 'magnetic' (manager-led) orchestration patterns. Reached 1.0 GA April 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge's sequential determinism is a deliberate design choice; concurrent/parallel execution (the main new capability here) was evaluated and deferred. A2A and group-chat patterns are not on the roadmap.

summary: LangGraph 1.2.16 adds per-call approvals, built-in MCP support, node timeouts, and DeltaChannel for typed streaming. LangChain 1.4 replaces AgentExecutor with create_agent wrapping LangGraph's engine.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — per-call approvals are already present via AwaitingPlanApproval gate; timeout handling exists; SSE streaming shipped. MCP is not part of AgentForge's CLI subprocess model.

source: ICLR 2026 MemAgents Workshop — episodic/semantic agent memory survey
summary: First major academic venue devoted to agent memory. Formalizes episodic (event tracking), semantic (fact storage), and working memory as three architectural pillars, with consolidation as a design pattern. Notes context windows do not replace external memory ('context rot').
relevanceToAgentForge: High — episodic run-outcome memory is already tracked by HID-188 (open issue). Skill distillation (semantic/procedural memory) has shipped. No new gap identified beyond what HID-188 already captures.

source: Prime Agent by Prime Intellect (Aug 2026, MIT License)
summary: Self-improving coding harness that revises outputs within the same session via a self-refining loop. Released August 6, 2026 under MIT license.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge's AddressingReview→AIReview loop already implements the equivalent within-session reflection cycle. Skill distillation captures cross-run improvements. No distinct gap identified.

summary: Academic coding agent that maintains an archive of prior agents with benchmark results; a meta-agent proposes improvements from the archive. Effectively a population-based self-improvement approach.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — the benchmark-archive-based meta-improvement model requires RL-style training infrastructure not present in AgentForge. The simpler within-session reflection pattern is already shipped. Cross-run meta-learning is tracked by HID-188.

summary: Self-improving agent with a headline reflection-based improvement loop. Reportedly crossed 90k GitHub stars within 2 months of launch. Self-improvement is the main differentiator vs prior frameworks.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the reflection loop pattern is what AgentForge's distillation pipeline approximates. The specific Hermes contribution is the scale of adoption showing the market demand. No new technical gap identified beyond HID-188.

summary: Small GitHub template implementing a Work→Complete→Reflect→Record loop that persists learnings to AGENTS.md and reusable skill files.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge ships this pattern via distillationAgent.ts + agentSkillRepository.ts. The AGENTS.md persistence model is similar to AgentForge's global skills. No gap.

source: Structured Output / JSON Validation Reliability best practices 2026
summary: 2026 practitioner consensus on structured output reliability: constrained decoding guarantees form not content; schema-enforced outputs + bounded retries with error feedback are the de facto standard. Zod/Pydantic validation + retry is recommended pattern.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge parses BEGIN/END_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT markers from CLI subprocesses. HID-167 already tracks automatic retry with failure classification. Bounded-retry-with-error-feedback could strengthen HID-167's scope but not a new issue.

source: ODYSSE: Episode-wise Policy Optimization for Personalized Agentic Reasoning (arXiv 2607.25369)
summary: RL-based policy optimization for personalizing agent reasoning over episodes. Uses episodic reward signals to adapt agent behavior per user context.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — RL training loop over agent episodes is in the red-flag disqualification list. Requires training infrastructure not present in AgentForge. Episodic memory aspect is already tracked by HID-188.

source: Deep Reasoning in General Purpose Agents via Structured Meta-Cognition (arXiv 2605.11388)
summary: May 2026 paper proposing structured meta-cognition as a mechanism for deep reasoning in general-purpose agents. Cites ReAct as prior work. Details on the specific architecture are not fully available from secondary sources.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — meta-cognition during planning could complement the planning stage; however the paper's specifics are unknown from current search results and the concept is complex. Needs direct reading before any issue could be scoped.
